paragraphs.en: THE SISTERS
paragraphs.zh: 姐妹们

paragraphs.en: There was no hope for him this time: it was the third stroke. Night after night I had passed the house (it was vacation time) and studied the lighted square of window: and night after night I had found it lighted in the same way, faintly and evenly. If he was dead, I thought, I would see the reflection of candles on the darkened blind for I knew that two candles must be set at the head of a corpse. He had often said to me: “I am not long for this world,” and I had thought his words idle. Now I knew they were true. Every night as I gazed up at the window I said softly to myself the word paralysis. It had always sounded strangely in my ears, like the word gnomon in the Euclid and the word simony in the Catechism. But now it sounded to me like the name of some maleficent and sinful being. It filled me with fear, and yet I longed to be nearer to it and to look upon its deadly work.
paragraphs.zh: 这次他没有希望了：这是他第三次中风。在假期期间，我每晚都经过那栋房子，观察着那扇亮着灯的方形窗户：每晚我都发现它以同样的方式亮着，微弱而均匀。如果他已经死了，我想，我会看到烛光在遮光窗帘上反射出来，因为我知道在尸体的头部必须点两支蜡烛。他曾经对我说过：“我不在这个世上待很久了”，我当时以为他的话是空话。现在我知道他是真的。每晚当我凝视着窗户时，我都会轻声对自己说那个词 瘫痪。这个词在我耳中一直听起来很奇怪，就像欧几里得中的“正切线”和《教理问答》中的“圣职买卖”一样。但现在，它对我来说仿佛成了某种邪恶而罪恶的存在。它让我感到恐惧，然而我又渴望更接近它，看看它那致命的作为。

paragraphs.en: Old Cotter was sitting at the fire, smoking, when I came downstairs to supper. While my aunt was ladling out my stirabout he said, as if returning to some former remark of his:
paragraphs.zh: 老科特坐在炉火旁抽烟，我下楼来吃晚饭的时候，他正坐在那里。当我姑妈正用勺子给我盛粥的时候，他说，仿佛是在回到他先前说过的话：

paragraphs.en: “No, I wouldn’t say he was exactly ... but there was something queer ... there was something uncanny about him. I’ll tell you my opinion....”
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不会说他完全是……但有某种怪异……有种诡异的感觉。我来告诉你我的看法……”

paragraphs.en: He began to puff at his pipe, no doubt arranging his opinion in his mind. Tiresome old fool! When we knew him first he used to be rather interesting, talking of faints and worms; but I soon grew tired of him and his endless stories about the distillery.
paragraphs.zh: 他开始抽起烟斗，毫无疑问是在心里整理自己的观点。真是个令人厌烦的老家伙！我们最初认识他的时候，他倒是挺有趣的，经常谈论昏厥和虫子；但我很快就对他感到厌倦了，他那些关于酿酒厂的没完没了的故事实在让人受不了。

paragraphs.en: “I have my own theory about it,” he said. “I think it was one of those ... peculiar cases.... But it’s hard to say....”
paragraphs.zh: “我对这件事有自己的看法，”他说，“我认为这是一起……特殊的情况……但很难说……”

paragraphs.en: He began to puff again at his pipe without giving us his theory. My uncle saw me staring and said to me:
paragraphs.zh: 他再次开始抽起烟斗，却没有把他的理论告诉我们。我叔叔看见我盯着他，便对我说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, so your old friend is gone, you’ll be sorry to hear.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，你那位老朋友走了，你听了应该会难过吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Who?” said I.
paragraphs.zh: “谁？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Father Flynn.”
paragraphs.zh: “弗莱恩神父。”

paragraphs.en: “Is he dead?”
paragraphs.zh: “他死了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Mr Cotter here has just told us. He was passing by the house.”
paragraphs.zh: “科特先生刚刚告诉我们。他路过那所房子。”

paragraphs.en: I knew that I was under observation so I continued eating as if the news had not interested me. My uncle explained to old Cotter.
paragraphs.zh: 我知道我正在被监视，所以我继续吃东西，好像这条新闻并没有引起我的兴趣。我叔叔向老科特解释道。

paragraphs.en: “The youngster and he were great friends. The old chap taught him a great deal, mind you; and they say he had a great wish for him.”
paragraphs.zh: “年轻人和他是非常要好的朋友。这位老先生教了他很多东西，而且据说他对这个年轻人怀有极大的期望。”

paragraphs.en: “God have mercy on his soul,” said my aunt piously.
paragraphs.zh: “上帝怜悯他的灵魂，”我姑妈虔诚地说。

paragraphs.en: Old Cotter looked at me for a while. I felt that his little beady black eyes were examining me but I would not satisfy him by looking up from my plate. He returned to his pipe and finally spat rudely into the grate.
paragraphs.zh: 老科特盯着我看了一会儿。我觉得他那双小而黑的眼睛在审视着我，但我不会让他得逞，于是继续低着头看着自己的盘子。他回到他的烟斗旁，最后粗鲁地往壁炉里吐了口痰。

paragraphs.en: “I wouldn’t like children of mine,” he said, “to have too much to say to a man like that.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不希望我的孩子和那种人有太多交往。”他说。

paragraphs.en: “How do you mean, Mr Cotter?” asked my aunt.
paragraphs.zh: “您是什么意思，科特先生？”我姑妈问道。

paragraphs.en: “What I mean is,” said old Cotter, “it’s bad for children. My idea is: let a young lad run about and play with young lads of his own age and not be.... Am I right, Jack?”
paragraphs.zh: “我的意思是，”老科特说，“这对孩子们不好。我的想法是：让一个年轻男孩和同龄的男孩们到处跑跑、玩玩，而不是……杰克，我说得对吗？”

paragraphs.en: “That’s my principle, too,” said my uncle. “Let him learn to box his corner. That’s what I’m always saying to that Rosicrucian there: take exercise. Why, when I was a nipper every morning of my life I had a cold bath, winter and summer. And that’s what stands to me now. Education is all very fine and large.... Mr Cotter might take a pick of that leg mutton,” he added to my aunt.
paragraphs.zh: “这也是我的原则，”我叔叔说，“让他学会在自己的角落里拼搏吧。我总是对那个玫瑰十字会的家伙这么说：要锻炼身体。要知道，我小时候，一生中每天早上都洗冷水澡，不管是冬天还是夏天。现在这对我还有好处呢。教育固然很好，很宏大……”他接着对我的婶婶说，“科特先生可以来点那条腿羊肉。”

paragraphs.en: “No, no, not for me,” said old Cotter.
paragraphs.zh: “不，不，不是给我。”老科特说。

paragraphs.en: My aunt brought the dish from the safe and put it on the table.
paragraphs.zh: 我姑姑从保险箱里拿出这道菜，放在了桌子上。

paragraphs.en: “But why do you think it’s not good for children, Mr Cotter?” she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “但是，科特先生，您为什么认为这对孩子不好呢？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: “It’s bad for children,” said old Cotter, “because their minds are so impressionable. When children see things like that, you know, it has an effect....”
paragraphs.zh: “这对孩子不好，”老科特说，“因为他们的思想很容易受影响。当孩子们看到那样的事情，你明白的，会产生影响……”

paragraphs.en: I crammed my mouth with stirabout for fear I might give utterance to my anger. Tiresome old red-nosed imbecile!
paragraphs.zh: 我嘴里塞满了粥，生怕自己会忍不住怒吼出来。这个讨厌的满脸通红的蠢货！
